summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000+ views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 50 views, so YouTube is barely working yet. The best videos are about robots and surprising 'it does the opposite of what you expect' sensors (gyro robot, clap switch, mic vs speaker), and they get the most likes and saves. Videos about everyday public places (lift door, mall door, taps, street light) and repeated topics (IR, smoke, taps twice) do poorly.
winningPattern: Hindi videos on a robot or a hands-on maker sensor, with a surprising, counter-intuitive hook ('X has no brain / can't hear / does the opposite'), a short punchy title with one emoji and #shorts, posted on Instagram Reels first. Newest posts (Oct 29 to Nov 2) are winning, so the maker/robot angle is trending up. 'Robot Deewar Se Kaise Bachta Hai' also led in shares (10), so robot problem-solving gets sent to friends.
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-project videos (gyro, line follower, obstacle avoidance) your main series
Open with a 'wrong belief' hook: 'X can't see/hear/think, yet it...'
Show a real build or demo in the first 2 seconds, then explain the part inside
Add a save-worthy ending, like a pin list or wiring tip, since saves drive the best videos
Test one YouTube-specific change: a bigger on-screen hook and a title without the question-mark style, and compare with Instagram
stopDoing: Stop making near-duplicate videos (two IR sensor, two smoke, three tap/door videos in a row)
Stop 'How does [public place thing] work?' titles for lifts, malls and street lights
Stop mixing in English videos without a plan: the one English upload has no Instagram reach
